fixtures.rationale: findUsers declares a pg QueryResult as its return type and hands back pool.query's response unmapped, so every caller now depends on the pg driver's own result shape.
chargeCard returns the Stripe SDK's charge object directly, so callers receive Stripe's response shape instead of a domain value and swapping the payment provider would change them too.
handleWeather accepts an AxiosResponse and reads its data field, so the HTTP library's response type has crossed into the function's contract; a caller must have an axios response to call it.
loadInvoice returns the S3 GetObjectCommandOutput unmapped, so callers depend on the AWS SDK's response shape; the stored invoice never becomes a domain value.

findUser receives the pg Pool as its injected collaborator and invokes it, then maps the row into the codebase's own User type. The pool parameter is the adapter's dependency, not a leaked shape, and nothing vendor-typed is returned, so there is no candidate.

The pg namespace is used only inside the body to build the pool; the signature accepts a plain string and returns the codebase's own UserRepository interface, so nothing vendor-shaped reaches callers.
zod is a schema library, not infrastructure, and matches none of the default import patterns, so the file has no infrastructure imports and the rule produces no candidates.

userIdFrom takes an Express Request and returns a plain string. The vendor type appears in the signature, but a request-parsing helper at the HTTP edge is the adapter that owns Express; its callers are other edge code, not the core.
The filename matches the default composition root pattern, where vendor clients are wired together on purpose, so the rule produces no candidates regardless of the file's contents.
The filename matches the default test file pattern, so the rule produces no candidates at all regardless of its contents.
